tasks.short: Coordinate fraud investigations with legal counsel and law enforcement.

steps.what: Collect case decisions, evidence references and outstanding questions for external coordination.
Draft a factual coordination brief and proposed disclosure list.

loop.input: Authorised coordination materials and a factual briefing template.
loop.output: Source-linked factual brief, proposed document list and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Verify every material statement against a source; counsel checks omissions and sensitive passages.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; missing support becomes an explicit question for the investigator.
loop.why_not_simpler: Case narratives and external questions vary; fixed templates alone cannot select and summarise relevant passages.

steps.what: Determine disclosure basis, privilege restrictions and permitted discussion boundaries.
Arrange a coordination meeting with the authorised external contacts.
Discuss evidence gaps, investigative sequencing and responsibilities with external counterparts.
Check recipients and transfer the permitted evidence pack through the agreed channel.
Record commitments, disclosure receipts and follow-up dates in the case register.

tasks.design: Use the restricted case register in the {WORKFLOW} to assemble source-linked coordination materials from the {DOCS}. A bounded loop drafts the factual brief; configured scheduling and controlled document sharing support the human conversation, with approval on invitations and evidence release.
tasks.previous_blocker: External coordination depends on trust, legal judgement and channels outside the company's control. Preparation and follow-up are mixed into the same correspondence.
tasks.enabler_now: Source-linked drafting and configured approval flows can reduce preparation and disclosure administration. No new capability replaces counsel or external relationships.
tasks.still_hard: Privilege, disclosure duties, investigative secrecy and cross-border transfers remain case-specific. GDPR and national procedural rules govern what may be shared and with whom.
tasks.human_edge: Negotiate sequencing, recognise an informal concern and preserve cooperation without compromising the investigation.
tasks.altitude: The investigator arrives better prepared and spends less time reconstructing commitments. Legal disclosure authority and relationships with external counterparts do not change.

loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per document; unreadable or conflicting records remain unresolved.

tasks.still_hard: Missing evidence, identity ambiguity, deliberate concealment, and fair interpretation remain expensive. GDPR and EU AI Act applicability require assessment; national rules govern employee investigations and consultation.
tasks.human_edge: The investigator tests innocent explanations, conducts fair interviews, and judges whether evidence supports an allegation.

tasks.short: Analyse financial records for irregularities and document supported findings.

Test duplicates, unusual billing patterns, financial links and procedural exceptions.
Inspect supporting evidence and assess alternative explanations for anomalies.

loop.input: Assessed anomalies, explanation notes and source-linked workpapers.
loop.output: Draft findings with evidence references, alternative explanations and explicit gaps.
loop.check: Populate figures from validated calculations; validate references; investigator checks meaning and unsupported claims.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per section; unresolved references or contradictions return to manual drafting.
loop.why_not_simpler: Calculations are deterministic, but varied explanations and evidential limitations require prose synthesis.

tasks.design: A governed job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reconciles financial exports and runs explicit tests, with source-linked exceptions shown in the {BI}. Investigators examine explanations and evidence; a bounded drafting loop creates the findings report in the {DOCS} for approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Joining exports and maintaining repeatable tests required specialist effort. Rules could surface known patterns but could not determine whether an anomaly represented fraud.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic pipelines, configurable dashboards and faster code development make repeatable testing easier to maintain. A bounded model loop can reduce report drafting effort while calculations stay outside the model.
tasks.still_hard: Collusion, changing schemes, poor identifiers and legitimate unusual transactions require investigation. Broad anomaly detection can create more review work than it saves.
tasks.human_edge: Develop hypotheses, challenge apparent patterns and distinguish suspicion from supported evidence.
tasks.altitude: The analyst spends more time testing explanations and proposing targeted control changes. They can recommend test changes more often; case closure and adverse-action authority remain unchanged.
